hints: Focus on atom conservation, since Al, Na, O, C and H must all balance even though you do not know the hydrocarbon yet.
Start with aluminium to fix the rest, 1 $\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3$ must make 4 $\text{NaAlO}_2$, so you need 4 $\text{NaOH}$ for Na balance.
Count O to find water, then count H and C together to see how many H must be shared among 3 carbons, remembering one molecule can be multiplied.
walkthrough:
**Balance the metals first**

Think like a detective. Aluminium and sodium are the easiest to lock down.

$$\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3 \rightarrow 4\,\text{NaAlO}_2$$

To get 4 Al on the right you need 4 of $\text{NaAlO}_2$. That also needs 4 Na, so you must use 4 $\text{NaOH}$ on the left.

**Use oxygen to find the water**

Now look at oxygen, because only $\text{NaOH}$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NaAlO}_2$ contain it.

$$\text{Left O: } 4 \text{ (from 4 NaOH)} + x \text{ (from } x\text{H}_2\text{O)} \quad = \quad \text{Right O: } 4 \times 2 = 8$$

So $x = 4$. You need 4 water molecules as reactants.

**Count H and C to identify the hydrocarbon**

Great, now count H on the left:

$$\text{H left} = 4 \text{ (from NaOH)} + 4 \times 2 = 12$$

All 12 H must end up in the hydrocarbon. All 3 C from $\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3$ must also end up there. So in total you need $\text{C}_3\text{H}_{12}$ worth of hydrocarbon.

No single $\text{C}_3$ alkane has 12 H, so it must be 3 small molecules: $3 \times \text{CH}_4$. The hydrocarbon itself is therefore $\text{CH}_4$.

Balanced check:
$$\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3 + 4\text{NaOH} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{NaAlO}_2 + 3\text{CH}_4$$

options.A: Correct. 3 molecules of $\text{CH}_4$ supply the required $\text{C}_3$ and $\text{H}_{12}$. This balances C, H, Al, Na and O perfectly with 4 $\text{NaOH}$ and 4 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ gives the wrong carbon count. You start with 3 C in $\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3$, so the hydrocarbon total must contain 3 C, not 2. This choice ignores carbon balance.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$ has the right number of carbons for one molecule, but only 8 H. The reaction supplies 12 H in total, so you are 4 H short. This is the trap of forgetting to balance oxygen with water first.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$ has far too many carbons. You only have 3 C available from $\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3$. This choice doubles the carbon and comes from guessing an alkene without doing atom balance.
